text:
Predicates:
CanRegisterVote(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateElection(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUSA(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTaiwan(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
ManagerAtGazprom(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir(x) ::: x is Vladimir.
Ekaterina(x) ::: x is Ekaterina.

Premises:
∀x (CanRegisterVote(x) → ParticipateElection(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the election.
CitizenshipUSA(x) → CanRegisterVote(x) ::: If someone has U.S. citizenship, then they can register to vote.
∀x (CitizenshipUSA(x) ∨ CitizenshipTaiwan(x)) ::: A person either has U.S. or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir does not hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬Official(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir is not a Russian Federation official.
¬HoldTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir) ∧ ¬ManagerAtGazprom(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegisterVote(Ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.

Conclusion:
CanRegisterVote(Ekaterina) ∨ ManagerAtGazprom(Ekaterina)
